text: Measured directly in the brain (7Li magnetic resonance spectroscopy, a small study of two volunteers at steady state), lithium's median half-life was 28 h there against 16 h in serum: the brain clears it more slowly than the blood does.
title: The brain lets go of lithium more slowly

text: Measured in post-mortem brain tissue of 11 treated patients (one small study, a population estimate), haloperidol sat at 10 to 30 times its optimal serum level and left the brain with a half-life of 6.8 days, against hours in the blood: its effects can outlast the last dose by weeks.
title: The brain lets go of haloperidol far more slowly

text: Paroxetine inactivates CYP2D6, the very enzyme that clears it (mechanism-based, or "suicide", inhibition), so it shuts down its own route of elimination. Plasma levels therefore rise more than in proportion to the dose. The substrate and inhibitor rows below describe a moving target, not a fixed rate.
title: Non-linear pharmacokinetics

text: MDMA inhibits CYP2D6, the enzyme that metabolises it (autoinhibition), so clearance saturates as the dose rises: the body removes a roughly fixed amount per hour instead of a fixed fraction (zero-order kinetics). Repeated doses therefore give disproportionately higher, longer-lasting levels. The substrate row below names the route, not its rate.
title: Non-linear pharmacokinetics

text: Nearly every pathway below is drawn twice, once in each hemisphere, because we assume the left and right brain are wired the same way. The sources describe a tract once, without saying which side, so the dataset stores one arrow and the viewer mirrors it onto the other hemisphere. No quote backs that mirrored copy, and a real pathway can be stronger on one side (lateralization). A mirrored pair counts as one fact in the sourcing tally, not two.
title: Left/right symmetry is assumed

text: Each enzyme above is sourced, but the list may be incomplete: it holds only the routes our sources happen to name, and none of them claims to name every one. A missing enzyme means no source named it, never that the drug avoids it. The interactions below are built from this same list, so a shared enzyme nobody named produces no interaction row.
title: Not the full set of routes
